research_scope: Source-free mathematical prerequisite identity audit against original formulation text; parent scope and stronger structural conditions remain distinct.

aliases.reason: The relative-global-complete-intersection source forms R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c), another instance of the general commutative ring quotient A/I. Only the quotient-ring prerequisite is shared; the specified coefficient ring, finitely generated polynomial relations and fibre-dimension constraints remain part of the original parent formulation.

An irreducible component V(p) for a prime p is a Zariski closed set in Spec(R) of the form V(I), here I=p; the support-of-a-finite-module statement also uses Zariski closed subsets V(I). Closedness of subsets in the prime spectrum is the same prerequisite, while minimality of p and the module-annihilator formula stay with their respective parent definitions.

Formally smooth and formally unramified ring-map statements both ask about lifting an R-algebra homomorphism f:S→A/I along the quotient q:A→A/I, i.e. g:S→A with q∘g=f. Smoothness requests existence, unramifiedness at-most-one; neither asserts both. This consolidates only the ordinary algebra-map-lift prerequisite.

Formal smoothness for K/k uses a k-algebra map K→A/I and a k-algebra lift K→A; this is precisely the ordinary R-algebra lifting diagram when R=k and S=K. Both source statements separately require square-zero ideals; uniqueness/existence, separability and field-extension properties remain distinct parent constraints.

The projective-module summand characterization invokes a binary external direct sum P⊕Q, which is the two-index instance of the general finite-support direct-sum construction ⊕_i M_i of R-modules. The direct-summand isomorphism P⊕Q≅R^(I) is a separate projectivity condition and is not identified with any arbitrary direct sum.
